unit.why: A short anecdote: before a journey the tsaddik hands his son his manuscript and names it 'Zikhron Devarim'; the name is later explained when most of the work is stolen.
unit.boundary_note: One of a numbered series of anecdotes about the same tsaddik; the 'journey mentioned above' refers back to an earlier division.

stories.end_quote: יפה צוה עליו אביו הרה״ק בשם זה
stories.summary_en: When parting from his son before a journey, the tsaddik gives him his manuscript to print and names it 'Zikhron Devarim'. The son is puzzled but too ashamed to ask. The manuscript is later neglected by his brother-in-law and most of its sermons are stolen, so that only 'a remembrance of words' remains, and the son then understands the name.

tags.why: The son, who narrates, and the brother-in-law are central.
The name implicitly foresaw the loss of most of the work.
The arc is a hidden foreknowledge that comes true.

quotes: ואז הבין כי יפה צוה עליו אביו
tags.why: The son later grasps the meaning of the name.
The son is afraid to ask.
He is too abashed to ask.
The tsaddik implicitly knows the fate of his book.
